native_result.query: How does incarceration affect the wealth of black individuals based on their income levels?
native_result.HypoA: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
native_result.HypoB: Incarceration exerts a statistically significant negative effect on the post-incarceration wealth of Black individuals across all baseline economic levels, with the largest absolute wealth penalty occurring among Black individuals at the highest baseline economic levels, who suffer substantial wealth erosion and net negative wealth accumulation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1. Filtered NLSY dataset for Black respondents (N=3,013). 2. Stratified sample into baseline economic tiers (Low, Middle, High) based on composite_wealth_1985. 3. Evaluated post-incarceration wealth (composite_wealth_1996) and wealth trajectory (1985-1996 growth) by incarceration status (ever_jailed) within each tier. 4. Conducted nonparametric tests (Mann-Whitney U), two-sample Welch t-tests, and OLS regression models with interaction terms controlling for sex and baseline wealth. 5. Synthesized findings into a data-grounded natural-language hypothesis.

sub_hypo.text: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.
sub_hypo.context: Black individuals, comparing the high-income group with those at lower wealth ranges.
sub_hypo.relations: Incarceration negatively affects wealth, but this negative effect may be smaller for the high-income group than for those at lower wealth ranges.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: The negative impact of incarceration on wealth for black individuals may be less for the high-income group than those at lower wealth ranges.

sub_hypo.text: Incarceration exerts a statistically significant negative effect on post-incarceration wealth among Black individuals across all baseline economic levels.
sub_hypo.context: Black respondents in the NLSY 1979 cohort (N=3,013), stratified into Low, Middle, and High economic tiers using 1985 composite wealth; incarceration occurred between 1985 and 1994, and post-incarceration wealth was measured in 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Incarceration has a statistically significant negative effect on 1996 composite wealth within every baseline economic tier, controlling for sex and baseline wealth.

sub_hypo.text: The largest absolute wealth penalty from incarceration occurs among Black individuals at the highest baseline economic levels, who experience substantial wealth erosion and net negative wealth accumulation.
sub_hypo.context: Black respondents in the NLSY 1979 cohort (N=3,013), comparing Low, Middle, and High tiers defined by 1985 composite wealth, with particular focus on the High tier; wealth trajectories span 1985–1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Baseline wealth modifies the incarceration-related wealth penalty: the High tier has the largest absolute penalty in 1996 wealth. Incarcerated Black respondents in this tier experience substantial wealth erosion, with 1996 wealth below 1985 wealth, yielding negative 1985–1996 wealth accumulation. Models control for sex and baseline wealth.
